⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Does any rule go *to* M1?" end="we can never use the transitions in M1" basis=The solver opens a branch questioning M1's reachability, explores all transitions, eliminates M1 as unreachable, and reuses this elimination to constrain the set of available transitions going forward.
⟦CYCLE⟧ trace=1 conf=probable start="What about $B, ...$?" end="So starting with B or C increases c." basis=The solver explores starting with B or C as an alternative to A, finds both increase c, eliminates them, and reuses the conclusion that A is necessary to minimize c early.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's double check this." end="This matches my derivation." basis=Re-executes the full level-by-level BFS analysis already completed earlier in the trace, reaching identical conclusions (min c=1 at L=1, c=1 at L=2, c=0 at L=3, c=-1 at L=4) with no new information.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="L=0: $\{(M0, 0)\}$" end="So length 4 is minimal." basis=Re-executes the BFS analysis a third time, reproducing the same state-by-state enumeration and conclusions with no new information or constraints.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's verify $AAAA$ again." end="The sequence is length 4." basis=Re-verifies the AAAA command sequence step by step, reproducing the same transition trace and conclusion already established earlier in the trace.
⟦LOOP⟧ trace=1 conf=clear start="Let's double check if M1 is really unreachable." end="Yes, no transition TO M1." basis=Re-verifies M1's unreachability by re-listing all transition rules, reaching the same conclusion already established earlier in the trace.
